verification.algorithm: SHA-256 (entry hashes and roots); Ed25519 (entry signatures)
instructions: 1. Sections: a LEDGER section is any object with rootHash and an entries array of ledger entries; a RECORD section is any object with rootHash and a records (or assets) array. Each has its own rootHash -- verify independently.

2. Ledger section rootHash = SHA-256 of its entries' entryHash values concatenated, in the order listed. Record section rootHash = SHA-256(JSON.stringify(records)); asset snapshots: SHA-256(JSON.stringify(assets)).

3. Recompute each ledger entry's entryHash: SHA-256 of the text 'invari.kos.ledger.entry.v4', a newline, then the canonical form of the entry without _id, entryHash and entrySignature (sorted keys; ObjectIds and dates appear as single-key $oid / $date objects and encode exactly as written).
4. Verify each entrySignature (Ed25519, base64) over the 32 raw bytes of entryHash with Invari's published public key for signingKeyId.

5. Chains: group entries by assetId, sort by version; versions must be contiguous and each previousEntryHash must equal the prior entry's entryHash. A chain may begin after v1 -- a firearm received from another licensee, or the exportRecord on Invari's ledger -- and its first previousEntryHash then points to an entry outside this file (join it with the previous holder's export).

6. masterRootHash = SHA-256 of every ledger section's rootHash followed by every record section's rootHash, each group in the order the sections appear in this file (kernel/tools/verifyExport.js applies this rule).

7. Signed records: a record in affirmationArtifacts or enforcementLog with sealFormatVersion 2 verifies like a ledger entry -- SHA-256 of its domain ('invari.kos.affirmation.record.v1' or 'invari.kos.enforcement.record.v1'), a newline, then the canonical form of the record without _id, entryHash and entrySignature; then its entrySignature with the published key for signingKeyId. A record without sealFormatVersion was written under an older, unsigned formula and verifies only by that (kernel/tools/verifyExport.js reports it as legacy).
verification.note: Ledger entries and signed records verify with only Invari's public key; no Invari infrastructure is required.
